reason: The text describes an external military attack by Amalek upon Israel (וַיָּבֹ֖א עֲמָלֵ֑ק וַיִּלָּ֥חֶם עִם־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל - 'And Amalek came and fought with Israel'). Israel does not initiate this conflict; rather, they respond defensively. The narrative emphasizes divine support for Israel's defense through Moses' raised staff and God's ultimate promise to defeat Amalek. There is no indication in this passage that Israel's suffering results from their own culpability or wrongdoing. The suffering is presented as an external aggression that Israel must resist, not as self-inflicted or a consequence of their own fault.
